question: What is formed right after a sperm successfully fertilizes an egg?
explanation: When the sperm and egg join, they combine their chromosomes to restore a full set of 46, creating a brand new single-celled zygote ready to grow! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h1)

question: In the human female reproductive tract, where does fertilization usually happen?

options.B: Lower third of the uterine cavity

explanation: The ampulla is the wider middle section of the fallopian tube and provides the perfect meeting place for the swimming sperm and the released egg. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h1)

question: What protective layer of cells surrounds a secondary oocyte when it is released during ovulation?
explanation: The corona radiata is a supportive halo of follicular cells wrapped around the egg that incoming sperm must work through during fertilization. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h2)

question: How do sperm mostly travel upward through the female reproductive tract?

options.A: Riding passively inside the bloodstream after vaginal absorption
options.B: Using their own flagellar motility and uterine muscle contractions
options.C: Crawling along the inner walls using specialized cilia
options.D: Being pushed entirely by gravity when the patient stands

explanation: While sperm use their tails (flagella) to swim, the smooth muscles of the uterus also squeeze rhythmically to help push them along on their journey. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h2)

question: What is the main goal of sperm capacitation inside the female reproductive tract?

options.A: To prepare the sperm membrane and make it capable of fertilizing the oocyte
options.B: To slow down sperm movement so they rest before reaching the egg
options.C: To increase the total volume of seminal fluid for easier transport
options.D: To attach extra chromosomes to the sperm tail for genetic diversity

explanation: Capacitation is like a final readiness training. It changes the sperm's membrane so it gains the strength to pierce the egg's outer layers. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h3)

question: What happens during the acrosome reaction when a sperm reaches the outer layers of an egg?

options.A: Enzymes are released from the sperm head to digest a path through protective layers
options.B: The sperm tail falls off completely to anchor the head inside the follicle
options.C: The egg swallows the entire sperm tail without using any chemical help
options.D: Protective antibodies coat the sperm to prevent premature entry

explanation: Think of the acrosome as a tiny chemical drill at the tip of the sperm head, releasing special enzymes to clear a pathway through the egg's defenses. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h3)

question: Which part of the sperm actually enters the inside (cytoplasm) of the egg during fertilization?

options.A: Only the tip of the flagellum
options.B: The head and core genetic contents
options.C: The acrosomal cap without any DNA
options.D: The entire intact sperm cell including its surface coat

explanation: Only the sperm's nucleus and inner contents enter the egg cytoplasm, while the outer membrane and tail stay behind. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h4)

question: Why is the initial binding between sperm and egg membrane proteins so important?

options.A: It immediately triggers the shedding of all female chromosomes
options.B: It stops the sperm from releasing any digestive enzymes
options.C: It ensures species-specific recognition before the cell membranes can fuse
options.D: It permanently seals the uterus against outside infections

explanation: The proteins act like a security check, making sure human sperm matches with a human egg before letting cell fusion happen. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h4)

question: What is polyspermy?

options.A: The rapid division of cells before implantation
options.B: The natural death of the oocyte inside the ovary
options.C: The fertilization of an oocyte by more than one sperm
options.D: The complete absence of sperm in the ejaculate

explanation: Polyspermy happens when multiple sperm enter an egg, which causes a dangerous overload of chromosomes that stops healthy development. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h5)

question: How does the slow block to polyspermy protect the newly formed zygote?

options.A: It hardens the zona pellucida so other sperm cannot penetrate
options.B: It destroys the genetic material of the first sperm
options.C: It closes the fallopian tube shut with scar tissue
options.D: It kills all remaining sperm inside the vaginal canal instantly

explanation: Once the first sperm gets inside, the egg quickly changes its outer shell (zona pellucida) into a tough shield so no other sperm can squeeze through. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h5)

question: What term describes the final coming together of the male and female genetic material (chromosomes)?
explanation: Syngamy is the exact moment the chromosomes from mum and dad finally mix together to form the unique genetic blueprint of the new baby. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h6)

question: What triggers a secondary oocyte to finish its second meiotic division?

options.A: The successful entry and fusion of a sperm cell
options.B: The complete shedding of the endometrial lining
options.C: A sudden drop in systemic progesterone levels
options.D: The physical passage of the egg through the cervix

explanation: The egg stays paused in its development process until a sperm successfully enters, giving it the green light to finish dividing. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h6)

question: What is the name of the hollow ball of cells that gets ready to implant in the uterus?
explanation: The blastocyst is the stage of early development that hatches from its outer shell and successfully nests into the lining of the womb. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h7)

question: Why do the very first cell divisions (cleavage) happen without the embryo getting physically larger?

options.A: The mother's bloodstream actively starves the embryo of extra water
options.B: The embryo remains constrained inside the protective zona pellucida
options.C: The fallopian tube physically compresses the cells to keep them small
options.D: Cells divide so quickly that they shrink in mass with every cycle

explanation: Because the tough outer shell (zona pellucida) doesn't stretch right away, the dividing cells simply pack tighter into smaller spaces until they are ready to hatch. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T1#GNS121_U6_T1_h7)
